title: Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM In

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The bullet list states: '(3) performing computations without upcasting to FP32 at runtime.' The very next sentence says: 'As illustrated in Figure 7, this approach ensures all computations occur in full FP32 precision...' The two statements are contradictory. If computations are not upcast to FP32, they cannot occur in FP32 precision. The intended method is to compute in FP32, so the bullet is incorrect.

Section 3.2 states: 'With FP32, almost all examples produce identical outputs across configurations, resulting in only 2.2% of the samples diverging' for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B on MATH500. Table 9 (Appendix) reports Div_Percent for the same model, dataset and precision as 5.80%, not 2.2%.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1 vs. Section 3.3 and Table 5 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3.1 describes the random-sampling evaluation: 'report the standard deviation of Pass@1 across 6 runtime configurations, varying GPU count (2 vs. 4) and numerical precision (BF16, FP16, FP32).' However, Section 3.3 and the caption of Table 5 clarify that the 6 configurations are (3 batch sizes × 2 GPU counts) per precision. The description in Section 3.1 is inconsistent with the actual design and with later explanations.

The text reads: 'Pass@1 evaluations use 4, 16, and 64 runs for MATH500 and AIME'24 respectively, without justification or confidence interval reporting, limiting statistical rigor.' This appears to be an editorial remnant (possibly from a review or author's note) that directly criticises the study's own statistical rigor. It is inconsistent with the paper's otherwise positive framing and should not appear in the final manuscript.

The paper claims: 'From a resource perspective, LayerCast offers substantial benefits over full FP32: memory usage is reduced by 34%...' No measurement data, experiment, or reference is provided to support this specific 34% figure. A careful reviewer would require evidence or removal of the unsupported number.
